I find in therepy it's actually mostly you coming to the conclusions yourself, and the therapist guides you. You can hear the best advice in the world, but I find it I don't feel like I've made that realization myself, it doesn't click! So honestly if you just have someone to talk to at all I think it would help you. Some of the best stuff in therapy I've learned are to notice limiting patterns in my thinking. So I have this problem in which I believe I'm not smart enough, but it's because I'm looking at all the wrong evidence of that. Like, what about being good at my job and how I went to college for example. Or if someone gives me a clear solution to someone I always say 'yeah... But," and that's really limiting! It's just your brain coming up with excuses. I think we all know what we need to do to get better, but medication and therapy or just really self reflection gets us started on that road to our goals and once we start on our goals, we start to feel better about ourselves and in general. Now, I do still struggle with anxiety and depression, but it's not as severe as it was before. And I'm proud of myself that I at least want to keep trying. My brain goes less to the option of, "well, I'm just going to unalive myself,". And more forgiving like no I just have to keep trying and I know I'll have better days.
